article.headline: SWIFT City: Sarjapura's Proposed Thousand-Acre Tech Township
paragraphs: SWIFT City stands for Startups, Work, Innovation, Finance and Tech. It is a Karnataka government proposal, handled by Commerce & Industries and KIADB, and it is at the announced stage.

The planned mix includes offices, co-working space, residential blocks and schools. The News Minute says plug-and-play facilities are planned for companies and start-ups. No investment figure, jobs target or timeline has been given.

As things stand, there is no evidence of approval or construction since the announcement. Anchors and road or rail connections have not been named, so the project is best read as a proposal rather than a scheduled build.

Sarjapura is already an established residential and office belt. If SWIFT City goes ahead, commentators could expect it to add to local demand for workspace and housing. That is an expectation only, and it depends on approvals and funding that have not been shown.
article.standfirst: The state's announced SWIFT City would bring offices, co-working, homes and schools to Sarjapura. Nothing yet shows approval or construction.
whats_next: Formal approval and a project cost

article.headline: Quantum City at Hesaraghatta Starts Small

key_facts.label: Components
key_facts.value: Hardware park, four innovation zones, FabLine

paragraphs: Quantum City, or Q-City, is a planned quantum technology cluster at Hesaraghatta, northwest of Bengaluru. It sits under the Karnataka Quantum Mission, run by the state government. Its stage is recorded as approved.
The planned components are a quantum hardware park, four innovation zones and a FabLine. No anchor tenants or jobs figure have been announced.
The Rs 1,000 crore figure is a budget allocation for the Karnataka Quantum Mission across the state. It is not a cost for the Q-City site alone. No site-specific cost has been given.

Hesaraghatta residents and buyers might expect a research cluster to draw skilled workers over time. That is a possibility, not a forecast. With only 6.17 acres sanctioned, the near-term footprint looks limited.
article.standfirst: Karnataka's Q-City has 6.17 acres sanctioned, a modest base for a project billed as a city and linked to a Rs 1,000 crore mission.

facts.excerpt: The state government has sanctioned 6.17 acres of land at Hesaraghatta
Announced under the ₹1,000 crore Karnataka Quantum Mission

article.headline: Bidadi AI Township Moves Ahead Amid Opposition
paragraphs: The Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township, also called the Bidadi AI Township, is a planned township around Bidadi in Ramanagara taluk. It covers nine revenue villages, including Byramangala, Hosur and Mandalahalli. The Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBDA) is the executing agency.
The News Minute reports an approved project cost of Rs 18,133 crore. The data records the project as under construction, though no completion date has been given. No jobs figure is available.

Supporters could point to the scale of the township as a potential driver of housing demand around Bidadi. Any such effect is an expectation. Litigation and land acquisition may affect how much of the plan is built, and when.
article.standfirst: The Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township spans 9,600 acres and carries an approved cost of Rs 18,133 crore, but farmers and political parties are contesting it.
whats_next: Progress on works and a completion timeline

The overall project cost, including land acquisition, is estimated at Rs 18,133 crore.

article.headline: KWIN City: A Knowledge Hub Planned Near Doddaballapura

key_facts.label: Roads
key_facts.value: NH 44, NH 648, Satellite Town Ring Road

paragraphs: KWIN City, short for Knowledge, Wellbeing and Innovation City, is a Karnataka government project. Its stated focus is education, research, health and start-ups. The scheme sits under the Commerce & Industries department and KIADB, and it is currently at the announced stage.
Its size is unclear. India Infra Hub reported it both as a 5,800-acre project and as 2,000 acres along the ring road. No investment figure has been given, so the project cost is not known.

Reported anchors include land offered for a Tata IISc Medical School, based on a search summary, and a 200-acre semiconductor park. Indian Infrastructure (July 2026) says the park is expected to be operational by December 2026 and to create 3,500 jobs. This date is an expectation, not a confirmed milestone.

Sources linking the project to nearby real estate describe it as a possible driver of demand around Doddaballapur. That is an expectation tied to announced plans, not a result. Buyers should note that acreage, cost and timelines are all still open.
article.standfirst: The state's proposed Knowledge, Wellbeing and Innovation City targets education, research, health and start-ups. Key details, including its acreage, are reported inconsistently.

article.headline: Harohalli Leads Options for Bengaluru's Second Airport
paragraphs: Bengaluru's second greenfield airport is a proposal. The Karnataka government and the Airports Authority of India (AAI) are involved. The project is at the proposed stage, with no approved design or budget.
No investment figure, jobs estimate or timeline has been reported. The only road link listed is Kanakapura Road. Anchors and rail connections have not been named.
The site has not been finalised, so other locations could still be chosen. Buyers should treat Harohalli as a candidate, not a decision.

Property commentators often expect that a confirmed airport would lift interest in surrounding areas. That is an expectation only. Without a final site, a cost and a timeline, it is too early to say what could happen near Harohalli.
article.standfirst: A 9,000-acre site at Harohalli on Kanakapura Road is the leading option for a second airport, but feasibility is pending and nothing is final.

facts.excerpt: Located about 40 km from the city centre
It is expected to span about 9,000 acres

article.headline: Dobbaspet Logistics Park Awarded, Land Still Pending
paragraphs: The Multi-Modal Logistics Park at Muddelinganahalli, near Dobbaspet in Bengaluru Rural, is a freight hub meant to link road and rail. It is being developed by NHLML, KIADB and an RVNL special-purpose vehicle, and abuts the national highway.

India Infra Hub puts the PPP estimated cost at Rs 1,770 crore. The project is structured as a DBFOT concession, and the stage is recorded as awarded. The PATH Bengaluru Logistics Park is named as an anchor.
Completion of land acquisition is listed as a risk. No opening date or jobs figure appears in the data, so the schedule is unclear.

Logistics parks tend to be discussed as possible drivers of warehousing and industrial land demand nearby. That is an expectation attributed to sector commentary, not a promise, and it will depend on the park becoming operational.
article.standfirst: The 400-acre Multi-Modal Logistics Park at Muddelinganahalli carries an estimated cost of Rs 1,770 crore and has been awarded.

facts.excerpt: The MMLP is being developed in an area of 400 acre
at an estimated cost of Rs 1,770 crore.

article.headline: Business Corridor Ring Road Reaches the Tender Stage
paragraphs: The Bengaluru Business Corridor, also known as the Peripheral Ring Road, is meant to link Hosur Road to Tumakuru Road around the edge of the city. Ballari Road is also listed among its connections. The scheme is led by the BDA through Bengaluru Business Corridor Ltd (BBCL).
The project is at the tendered stage, which means works have not been confirmed as started. Two earlier tenders failed, a risk for any buyer assuming a firm schedule.

If the corridor is built, some observers expect it to improve access to localities along Hosur Road, Tumakuru Road and Ballari Road. That is an expectation attributed to sources, not a promise. Tender outcomes will decide how soon it matters.
article.standfirst: The 1,950-acre Bengaluru Business Corridor, an approved Rs 3,348 crore scheme, is being tendered after two earlier tenders failed.

facts.excerpt: The estimated project cost for this stretch stands at Rs 3,348 crore.
The construction timeline for the package has been set at 36 months.
The Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA) has allocated 1,950 acres for the project

clusters.location_text: Hosur Road to Tumakuru Road, around the city periphery
clusters.name: Bengaluru Business Corridor

article.headline: Karanth Layout: 18,400 Sites Reserved for Landowners
paragraphs: Dr K. Shivaram Karanth Layout is a residential layout developed by the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) in north Bengaluru. The data records its stage as under construction.
The data does not give the layout's area, project cost, completion date or road connections. Readers should not assume any of these from the site count alone.
Litigation is a recorded risk. The layout has a history of court cases, which could affect timelines and the allotment process.

For nearby real estate, any effect is an expectation rather than a certainty. A completed, well-connected layout could add to housing supply in north Bengaluru, but the available facts do not show when that will happen.
article.standfirst: The BDA's Dr K. Shivaram Karanth Layout in north Bengaluru is under construction, with a large block of sites set aside for landowners.

facts.excerpt: 18,400 sites have been reserved for farmers and landowners who surrendered their land for the layout project.
